items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-120518 (score CVSS 9.1).

The BuddyPress XProfile Image Field plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.0. This is due to bpxp_image_field_update_on_user_activation() calling unlink() on a path built from visitor-supplied signup metadata with no realpath() resolution, no containment check against the profile-image directory and no extension allow-list. Submitting a zero-byte file with the 'field_N_hidden' parameter during registration makes the plugin store the raw value, which is then resolved against the document root when the pending signup is activated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file (such as wp-config.php) is deleted. Requires open registration and an image-type profile field on the signup form.

Score CVSS : 9.1

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-22

All three surfaces share the same root cause (the missing # escape in the Ruby double-quoted-string emission path) and are addressed by the same patch:

Both flows are automated in the reproduction script submitted with the original report and were verified against Ruby 3.x.

Le collectif de hackers LunarisSec affirme avoir découvert une vulnérabilité permettant d’accéder à des documents PDF contenant des informations personnelles et commerciales de clients.

Dans un échange avec Cyberattaque.org, LunarisSec indique que 1 699 factures seraient concernées et affirme que la faille de sécurité est toujours ouverte au 3 novembre 2026. Selon le collectif, les documents resteraient donc accessibles.

Implantée à Sénas, dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, JASP-K9 est une société privée qui propose notamment des écussons, vêtements, accessoires et équipements personnalisés pour les policiers, gendarmes, militaires, pompiers ou encore les unités cynophiles.

Il ne s’agit donc pas d’un site officiel de la Police nationale ou de la Gendarmerie nationale , mais d’un commerce spécialisé dans des produits pouvant être achetés aussi bien par des professionnels que par d’autres clients. Cette distinction est importante pour comprendre la portée de l’incident revendiqué.

Dans une publication diffusée sur X, le collectif LunarisSec affirme avoir identifié une faiblesse de sécurité permettant de consulter des documents de facturation associés à JASP-K9.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Members of Germany's political elite were among the spyware targets in 99 countries that Apple personally warned recently.

Multiple lawmakers and public figures in Germany are among the snooping victims Apple warned last week about spyware attacks, according to the country’s information security agency.

The hacking attempts are a significant development underscoring the national security threat European officials face as spyware deployment becomes both increasingly visible and apparently inexorable under current policies on the continent.

They also spotlight Europe’s continuing vulnerability to snooping, which human rights and digital freedoms advocates have loudly demanded lawmakers address more aggressively.

On Monday, the German news magazine Der Spiegel reported the Apple threat notifications were sent to members of a German delegation of federal ministries’ staffers, lawmakers and journalists traveling with Chancellor Friedrich Merz on a sweep through Asia. While there Merz met with top officials in South Korea, Japan and Singapore.

Many of the victims have not come forward, but on Tuesday morning, Franziska Brantner, co-leader of the Green Party and a member of the parliament’s European Affairs Committee, revealed she was among the victims, whom Apple said were located in 99 countries.

The information security agency, known as the BSI, on Friday sent German officials, lawmakers and public figures who received the threat notifications a warning letter saying they should assume their devices are infected and immediately replace them, according to a local news outlet’s interview with Digital Minister Karsten Wildberg.

Google along with several cybersecurity companies and Japanese law enforcement dismantled a global botnet called X.CPE that was hidden in more than 1.3 million set-top boxes across more than 200 countries.

Google said it tied the scheme to Videostrong Technology, a Chinese company that was an Android original equipment manufacturer producing a range of screens, speakers and robots.

The overwhelming majority of the infected devices in the X.CPE botnet are Android TV set-top boxes, Google said, adding that they observed a number of other infected Android-based IoT devices, including telehealth devices, karaoke machines and digital signage devices.

In lengthy reports about the scheme, Google and other cyber investigators accused Videostrong of monetizing the backdoor by “selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices.”

“We found this malicious software built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years, supported by dedicated infrastructure and constantly evolving configurations to evade detection and manage their affiliates,” Google said.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Hacker News.

Google details LLMjacking attacks that hijack enterprise AI resources, generating fraudulent cloud charges reaching $1 million at some organizations.

Google on Monday warned that threat actors are hijacking enterprise access to Large Language Models (LLMs) to fraudulently leverage expensive computing resources and AI services.

The tactic is called LLMjacking , a form of resource hijacking adapted for the LLM era, where an attacker obtains an API key through phishing, source code leaks, misconfigured environments, or exposed client-side code to gain unauthorized access to an organization's LLM accounts, while the legitimate owner covers the consumption costs.

Such attacks have a wide geographical footprint, with impacted entities located in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors.

"Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours," Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant said in a report shared with The Hacker News.

On one end of the spectrum are low-level resource theft that involves the manipulation of customer support chatbots to conduct unauthorized tasks like code generation. LLMjacking is on the other end, as they target the backend model resources directly by identifying publicly exposed LLM endpoints or obtaining valid LLM API keys.

Signal de veille — The Record.

Russia's Interior Ministry said Monday that police had dismantled the group's infrastructure and identified its suspected members following an investigation conducted with assistance from cybersecurity firm Kaspersky.

Russian authorities have arrested three suspected members of a cybercriminal group known as VasyGrek in a rare public crackdown on a long-running Russian-speaking hacking operation.

The group, also known as Fluffy Wolf, has been active since at least 2016 and has primarily targeted Russian companies with phishing emails designed to steal credentials, gain access to corporate networks and deploy malware.

Russia's Interior Ministry said Monday that police had dismantled the group's infrastructure and identified its suspected members following an investigation conducted with assistance from cybersecurity firm Kaspersky.

The group's alleged leader has been placed under house arrest, while two suspected accomplices have been released under travel restrictions, according to ministry spokesperson Irina Volk.

Such arrests are unusual in Russia, where many well-known Russian-speaking hacking groups have operated for years despite being closely monitored by cybersecurity researchers and law enforcement agencies.

Volk said the group's activities had attracted the attention of law enforcement agencies in Russia, the United States and Europe, but did not elaborate on whether foreign authorities had assisted in the investigation.
